text:
maria_cs: FYI customer (AcmeCorp) hit 403 on /v1/rerank yesterday after rotating keys. same API key still returns embeddings fine.

alex_infra: can you paste the raw request/response? headers, token claim sample, etc.

maria_cs: here's the snippet they shared:
```
POST /v1/rerank HTTP/1.1
Host: api.redwood.ai
Authorization: Bearer <redacted>
Content-Type: application/json

{ \"queries\": [...], \"candidates\": [...] }
```
Response: 403 {\"error\":\"insufficient_scope\", \"detail\":\"missing:rerank\" }

jordan_support: they also ran `/v1/embeddings` with same token and it works (200). customer says rotation script uses our CLI to provision.

sam_security: interesting — provisioning normally yields scopes as an array in the JWT claim `entitlements` or `scopes`. ask for the decoded JWT.

maria_cs: they sent decoded claims (redacted):
```json
{
  "sub": "svc-acme-01",
  "scopes": "infer embeddings",
  "iat": 1710650000
}
```
Note: `rerank` missing. customer insists the provisioner passed `infer,embeddings,rerank` though.

alex_infra: Aha. Could be our auth proxy sanitizer that normalizes separators. We had a recent change to strip non-alphanum characters and collapse comma/semicolon into spaces. If the provisioner sent `rerank\n` or `rerank\r` it might have been dropped.

maria_cs: customer shared the raw provisioning payload log (excerpt):
```
scopes: "infer, embeddings, rerank\n"
```
They think newline got appended by their deployment script.

sam_security: Repro steps I recommend: 1) curl our token introspect endpoint with the key, 2) look at `x-forwarded-scope` header at the edge gateway, 3) check the JWT stored in auth DB.

alex_infra: quick repro I ran locally emulating the gateway sanitizer:
```bash
$ printf 'infer, embeddings, rerank\n' | sed 's/[^a-z0-9 ,]//g' | tr ',' ' ' | tr -s ' '\n# -> "infer embeddings rerank"  (ok)
# but if sanitizer removed trailing token due to newline parse bug -> "infer embeddings"
```
Looks like a small parse bug if trailing newline isn't handled in one code path.

jordan_support: customer wants a hotfix. what's the mitigation?

alex_infra: short-term: create a new key via the admin console (UI strips newlines safely) and confirm it has `rerank`. Or tell customer to re-run provisioner removing trailing newline. I'll open an infra ticket for the sanitizer.

devops-bot: Created INCIDENT-3782: "edge-gateway-sanitize-trailing-newline-drops-scope" assigned to @alex_infra. <https://go.redwood/INCIDENT-3782> :rotating_light:

sam_security: long-term: make scope parsing strict and add unit test for newline/CR handling + add logging when claims differ between ingress header and stored JWT.

maria_cs: shared suggested customer message: "we rotated and reprovisioned via UI, rerank now works — thanks for quick triage." customer asked for ETA on patch.

alex_infra: ETA for patch: I can ship a patch to the gateway sanitizer today, deploy to canary in ~2h, full rollout later if canary looks good. Will post updates in INCIDENT-3782.

jordan_support: tagging @sam_security for approval on logging changes so we don't leak scopes in logs.

sam_security: yes keep logs redacted, only emit a boolean mismatch flag.

maria_cs: marking customer case as "workaround applied" and will follow up after the deploy. :thumbsup:

alex_infra: quick note for postmortem: add a tiny e2e that provisions keys with weird whitespace/CR and asserts scopes preserved.

jordan_support: closing loop — customer confirmed new key fixed it 10m after we advised. will keep thread open until deployment complete.
